The renter or buyer will place a deposit or premium (which is not the same as a security deposit) to obtain the option (the right) to buy the home at a future date for a specific price. The renter or buyer often pays extra rent in addition to the market rent. This additional rent is frequently designated to be applied toward the purchase price of the home.
The contract typically includes an "option" to purchase; it does not usually require the renter to buy the home. The purchase price is negotiated before any agreements are signed, and the option to buy is generally available to the renter for the duration of the lease contract (for example, if the lease is for 12 months, the renter can choose to buy at any time during that period).
Typically, a rent-to-own agreement is technically a lease-option contract, where you lease the property for a fixed duration and have the option to buy it at a discounted price during the lease term. 
It is important to note that "rent to own" is not a standard agreement; it can vary based on what the seller and renter agree upon. Most sellers may prefer to receive their money in full to purchase their next home. However, you may find an investor willing to work with you, but it may come at an inflated price, higher interest rate, or both.

history.content: What options are available for a home loan with poor credit but a good rental history?
Sorry, but I do not know.
Are there any options available that require no down payment?

Yes. If you're in the US, several options allow you to buy a home with little to no down payment. However, you will still need some funds for closing costs, which can often be negotiated with the seller. 
One option is an FHA loan, which requires a down payment of only 3.5%. The US government effectively subsidizes the remainder of your down payment. Other options include 80/20 loans, which provide 100% coverage, and HUD assistance programs, which can help you secure a 100% loan through FHA.
Can I get an FHA loan if I have a low credit score?
Yes, you can qualify for their loan programs with a credit score as low as 580.
Do I need to pay for PMI with an FHA loan?

Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is required for FHA loans with less than 20% equity. PMI must accompany FHA-insured loans because the FHA element serves as the insurance. The FHA does not provide the loan; instead, it insures the loan on behalf of a lender. This arrangement comes at a cost to the borrower. Still, it allows individuals who may struggle to afford a traditional mortgage to qualify, thanks to lower payment requirements and a reduced PMI.
What is MMI or Mutual Mortgage Insurance?
MI stands for Mortgage Insurance, which is a generic term. FHA refers to MMI, or Mutual Mortgage Insurance.
Is there a maximum income limit to qualify?
I do not know if there is a maximum income limit for qualifying for an FHA loan.

statements: Rent-to-buy typically involves paying an upfront deposit or premium to purchase the right to buy a home later at a specified price.
The upfront deposit or premium in a rent-to-buy arrangement is separate from a security deposit.
Rent-to-buy arrangements often require rent payments above the market rate.
The rent paid above the market rate may be contractually credited toward the purchase price.
The document notes that many people recommend applying the rent paid above the market rate specifically toward the down payment.
Rent-to-buy is not necessarily an option without upfront payments.
The document does not establish whether poor credit affects eligibility for a rent-to-buy arrangement.
The document does not establish whether a good rental history helps with eligibility for a rent-to-buy arrangement.
The document does not establish whether a rent-to-buy arrangement guarantees access to financing at the time of purchase.
